findings.title: Digest / identity
findings.privateFieldInsideDigestMaterial: CONFIRMED. `canonicalizeEventDigestV1` material includes `payload: event.payload` -- src/lib/events/journal/EventJournalCanonicalizer.ts:211 -- and `sourcePrivate` is a key ON that payload (JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:185 `payload: sourcePrivate === null ? base : { ...base, sourcePrivate }`). EventJournalCanonicalizer.ts is NOT in the stack diff (`git diff --name-only b7d650997 10a60ae5` lists 5 files, none of them the canonicalizer), so the digest contract is unchanged as the spec requires.
findings.legacyByteIdentity: CONFIRMED. src/lib/campaign/sync/__tests__/JournalCampaignEventStore.test.ts, row 'leaves a legacy envelope byte-identical and its digests unchanged', asserts three things on a real cold-reopened SQLite row: `expect(Object.hasOwn(stored.payload, 'sourcePrivate')).toBe(false)` (conditional absence -- not `{}`, not an enumerable `undefined`), `expect(canonicalizeJsonV1(stored.payload)).toBe(LEGACY_CANONICAL_PAYLOAD)` (byte pin), and `expect(stored.eventDigest).toBe(LEGACY_EVENT_DIGEST)`.
findings.byteProvenance: The LEGACY_CANONICAL_PAYLOAD literal is `{"campaignEvent":{...},"expectedPostStateDigest":null,"intentFingerprint":null}` -- exactly the three keys the BASE constructed, which I confirmed against the removed lines of the S1 diff (`- payload: { campaignEvent: event, expectedPostStateDigest, intentFingerprint }`). The pin is therefore verifiable by inspection against the base shape regardless of how it was captured; it does not rest on trusting the capture.
findings.digestProvenanceIndependentCheck: I independently recomputed LEGACY_STATE_DIGEST in this session with plain node (sorted-key canonical JSON + sha256 over UTF-8 bytes, replicating EventJournalCanonicalizer.ts:59-121 and JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:138-142): got `b05fc8809b072a0ce1c2a189ad2018be1ca566fa43fd1a77b54824bd135063bc`, identical to the pinned literal. So that value is a real digest, not a fabricated or self-recomputed placeholder.
findings.unverified: UNVERIFIED: I did not independently re-derive LEGACY_EVENT_DIGEST (`061d860f...`). Its canonical material has 22 fields including a derived eventId, commitPosition and recordedAt (EventJournalCanonicalizer.ts:187-212), and reconstructing it outside the test harness was not worth the cost -- because it is not the load-bearing pin. The canonical-payload byte string is, and that one IS independently inspectable. The event-digest pin is a corroborating whole-material pin; its base-capture provenance rests on the author's claim.
findings.identityCommitmentRow: CONFIRMED. src/lib/campaign/delivery/__tests__/projectCampaignStreamForGrant.test.ts, row 'still commits the delivered identity to the whole stored payload': asserts `Object.hasOwn(rows[0].payload, 'sourcePrivate') === true` and then reads the durable mapping directly -- `SELECT projected_event_identity AS identity FROM delivery_event_mapping WHERE delivery_epoch_id = ?` -- asserting `identities.map(r => r.identity)` equals `[rows[0].eventDigest]`. This is exactly the accepted RE-4 residual pinned as EXPECTED rather than hidden: only the one-way commitment crosses, never the values.

findings.title: Replay (S2)
findings.result: PASS on the fold and the cold reopen; GAP on the typed refusals (see RQ-1)
findings.foldsFromSourceRecordBodyNotCompactGenes: CONFIRMED. `replayCampaignSourceContracts` (campaignSourcePrivateEnvelope.ts:214-243) collects private facts in row order, takes `facts[0]` as the baseline, then at :229-233 `JSON.parse(first.baseline.sourceRecordBody)` and reads `parsed.contractMarket` through `rehydrateContractMarket` as `baselineMarket`. It never reads a CampaignSnapshotPublished, and `campaignSourceGenesis` is not imported. Pinned behaviourally by the S2 row: `baselineMarket.offers` maps to `['offer-remaining','offer-taken']` -- BOTH offers, which exist only in the persisted body -- while `remainingMarket.offers` is `['offer-remaining']`, the post-acceptance fold. A compact-genesis baseline would have produced an empty market, so the assertion discriminates.
findings.coldReopenAtRealSQLiteBoundary: CONFIRMED and genuine. The suite mkdtempSync's a real temp directory, opens a file-backed `new Database(file)` with `journal_mode = WAL` and `foreign_keys = ON`, runs `EVENT_JOURNAL_MIGRATION.up`, appends, then `first.close()` -- and only then `openJournal(file)` constructs a brand-new `Database` handle and re-reads via `readStream`. Nothing in-process survives the boundary.
findings.typedRefusalsImplemented: campaignSourcePrivateEnvelope.ts:85-103 defines `CampaignSourcePrivateReplayReason` = 'unsupported-schema' | 'source-identity-mismatch' | 'no-private-payload' and the `CampaignSourcePrivateReplayError` class; raised at :160-165 (schema), :171-176 (baseline digest), :223-228 (empty stream). None of the three returns a compact fallback -- every one throws.
findings.typedRefusalsProven: NO -- zero coverage. See requiredEdits RQ-1. Also uncovered: the skip-rows-without-a-private-payload branch at :220 (`if (found !== null) facts.push(found)`; every row in the one replay fixture carries a payload), the `?? stamped.remainingMarket` fallback at :183-184, and the `EMPTY_MARKET` fallback at :233.
findings.noSilentFallbackToCompact: CONFIRMED BY READING, UNPROVEN BY TEST. There is no code path in the module that degrades to the compact projection -- grep shows no import of any wire projector and no `campaignEvent` read. The guarantee is structurally sound; it is the regression guard that is missing.

findings.title: Money / serialization round-trip fidelity
findings.money: LOSSLESS, verified by reading both halves. `Money.toJSON(): number { return this.amount; }` (src/types/campaign/Money.ts:113-115) where `get amount() { return this.cents / 100; }` (:27-29); the inverse `constructor(amount) { this.cents = Math.round(amount * 100); }` (:19-22). round(x/100*100) === x for any integer cents, so the JSON number round-trips to the identical cents value. Rehydration accepts all three historical shapes -- Money instance, bare number, `{amount}`, `{centsValue}` -- at missionSerialization.ts:19-27. Pinned live by the S2 row: `expect(recovered.paymentTerms.basePayment).toBeInstanceOf(Money)` and `expect(recovered.paymentTerms.basePayment.amount).toBe(1_250_000)` after a real cold SQLite reopen.
findings.dates: NO DATE LOSS POSSIBLE. Every temporal field on IContract is an ISO-8601 STRING, not a Date instance -- `readonly createdAt: string` / `readonly updatedAt: string` / `readonly startDate?: string` / `readonly endDate?: string` (src/types/campaign/Mission.ts:102-111). JSON.stringify/parse is the identity on strings. There is no Date anywhere in IContract, IPaymentTerms or ICampaignContractMarket, so the classic Date->string asymmetry does not arise.
findings.otherNonJsonSafeTypes: NONE. A field-by-field read of IMission/IContract (Mission.ts:85-175) finds only strings, numbers, booleans, string enums, `readonly string[]`, and IPaymentTerms (the Money carrier). No Map, no Set, no class other than Money. `ICampaignContractMarket` is `{ offers: IContract[], declinedOfferIds: string[] }`.
findings.documentedLoss: `toJsonSafe` (campaignSourcePrivateEnvelope.ts:122-124) drops keys whose value is `undefined` -- stated in its own comment at :117-121 and REQUIRED, because canonicalizeJsonV1 rejects `undefined` outright (EventJournalCanonicalizer.ts:74-77, the `default: fail('unsupported-value')` arm). For `readonly foo?: T` optionals, absent and undefined are the same value, so this is not a fidelity loss.
findings.caveat: See OB-4: `rehydrateCampaignMission` silently returns its input un-rehydrated when `isContract()` fails, so a corrupt stored contract degrades quietly rather than refusing. Untested, low reachability.

findings.title: Falsification -- is S3's routing load-bearing?
findings.result: PASS -- F1 red 1:1, F2 vacuously green; the routing is load-bearing
findings.method: I did NOT re-run the mutations myself: the review is read-only and the worktree had to be returned clean on the S3 branch. I opened and read both author logs in full and cross-checked their internal content against the code, which is self-corroborating (the F1 failure text contains the actual leaked bytes, which cannot be fabricated by a log that merely claims a failure).

F1.label: envelopeOf's narrowing deleted (siblings ride along) WITH the S3 routing in place
F1.summaryLine: Test Suites: 2 failed, 2 total / Tests: 6 failed, 16 passed, 22 total
F1.bothLeakRowsRed: YES. The failing-test list contains BOTH `projectCampaignStreamForGrant source-only private envelope > withholds the private contract and market from a restricted campaign-scope guest` AND `... from a GM all-scopes grant`, plus the compact-narrowing assertion in the cold-reopen row and 3 collateral contract rows.
F1.quotedEvidence: The restricted-guest failure prints the actual delivered page: `Expected substring: not "house-liao" / Received string: "[{\"deliverySequence\":1,\"event\":{\"campaignEvent\":{...},\"expectedPostStateDigest\":null,\"intentFingerprint\":null,\"sourcePrivate\":{\"acceptedContract\":{...\"targetId\":\"house-liao\"...},\"baseline\":{...\"sourceRecordBody\":\"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"campaign-private-leak\\\"}\"...},\"remainingMarket\":{...\"offer-remaining\"...},\"schemaVersion\":1}...}}]"` -- i.e. the entire private envelope reaches a campaign-scope guest's delivery page once the narrowing is gone. That is a true 1:1 falsification, not a proxy assertion.

F2.label: the SAME envelopeOf mutation, but projectCampaignStreamForGrant reverted to the PRE-S3 inline narrowing
F2.summaryLine: Test Suites: 1 passed, 1 total / Tests: 6 skipped, 2 passed, 8 total -- `withholds ... from a restricted campaign-scope guest` PASSED, `withholds ... from a GM all-scopes grant` PASSED
F2.conclusion: VACUOUS WITHOUT S3. With the old inline `stored.payload.campaignEvent` at :252, deleting envelopeOf's narrowing leaves both leak rows green -- the rows would have been proving nothing about the boundary they claim to guard. This is the measured confirmation that the prior review's RE-2 finding was correct and that S3 is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.

rq1Assessment.result: DISCHARGED -- the required edit is satisfied in full and the rows are NOT tautological
rq1Assessment.diffRead: git diff 6dfddf79870465ae68545bc038b40626f22284fd 8f7f79d850cd526fa0eb6b52e389ecd59caa8a8b -- read in full in this session.
whyNonTautological: STRICTNESS OF THE HELPER. `refusalReasonOf(read)` calls the read inside a try, RETURNS `error.reason` only when the caught value `instanceof CampaignSourcePrivateReplayError`, RETHROWS anything else (so a TypeError fails the row rather than passing it), and -- the load-bearing part -- `throw new Error('expected a typed replay refusal, but the read returned')` on the no-throw path. A silent compact fallback RETURNS, so it fails here. This is exactly the regression RQ-1 named.

BOTH FORMS ASSERTED. Each row does `expect(() => read()).toThrow(CampaignSourcePrivateReplayError)` AND `expect(refusalReasonOf(() => read())).toBe('<reason>')`. The class pin distinguishes a refusal from a crash; the reason pin distinguishes the three refusals from each other, so a row cannot pass on the wrong branch.

REAL PERSISTENCE BOUNDARY, NOT AN OBJECT LITERAL. The `storePrivate(name, sourcePrivate)` helper commits the corrupted payload through `appendCampaignCommandBatch` into a file-backed SQLite journal (`journal_mode = WAL`, `foreign_keys = ON`, `EVENT_JOURNAL_MIGRATION.up`), asserts `committed.kind === 'committed'`, CLOSES the handle, then re-opens a fresh `Database` and reads the row back via `readStream`. The corruption therefore survives canonicalization and persistence -- the reader is not handed a hand-built object.

ONE-FIELD ISOLATION. `wellFormedPrivate()` builds a valid payload and each row overrides exactly ONE field by spread: `schemaVersion: built.schemaVersion + 1` for row 1, `baseline: { ...built.baseline, sourceBodyDigest: 'f'.repeat(64) }` for row 2. Because `campaignSourcePrivateOf` checks schema first (campaignSourcePrivateEnvelope.ts:160-165) and the digest second (:171-176), row 2's correct schemaVersion is what makes the digest branch reachable at all. Each row proves its own branch, not merely 'something threw'.

ROW 3 USES A GENUINELY EMPTY-OF-PRIVATE STREAM. It commits `hireBatch(0)` (a real two-event batch) with NO `sourcePrivate`, asserts `rows` has length 2, then requires `replayCampaignSourceContracts(rows)` to refuse with `'no-private-payload'`. That also incidentally covers the previously-uncovered skip-rows-without-a-payload branch at campaignSourcePrivateEnvelope.ts:220, since both rows are skipped before `facts[0]` is found undefined.
